question: On the 18 partsheet_tolerance pictures, are the AI agent readers the odd one out (rows vs not rows), or do two people disagree as much?
pictures: the same 18 pictures, page and calls as partsheet_tolerance (8 levels, 8 level blanks, calibration + its blank)
readers: agent majority (binary majority of the 3 valid agent readers of each exact tile; the calibration pair: the 3 agent readers of the field-size screen)

rule.calls: every call binary: rows vs not rows (strokes and nothing are both not rows); the partsheet blank mask is NOT applied
rule.valid_chris: calibration rows and at most 1 of the 9 blanks rows; else UNDECIDED (that is the finding)
rule.discordant: pictures where Sebastien and the agent majority differ (expected 5 of 18, checked at Stage 0)
rule.k: on the discordant pictures, how many times Chris sides with Sebastien
rule.m: on the concordant pictures, how many times Chris differs from both

decision.HUMANS-NOISY: every other outcome (including m >= 2 at any k, and k = 2-3)

rule.gap_free: every (k, m) has exactly one verdict; the bars are written for 5 discordant / 13 concordant pictures
rule.timing: Chris's rating file must be later than the prereg's first commit; otherwise the numbers are descriptive only
rule.stage0: 18 pictures; 3 valid agent readers per picture and 0 ties; 5 Sebastien-agent disagreements; Sebastien valid; else INCONCLUSIVE by Stage 0
rule.descriptive: exact sign test on k of 5 (cannot fall below 0.031 one-sided / 0.0625 two-sided); Cohen's kappa per pair; raw agreement of 18; the same k / m on levels + calibration only

scope: no outcome makes the agents the reading instrument; HUMANS-NOISY means lines resting on one rater are labelled 'one rater' and a claimed read needs two raters
